name: Popliteus
description: Flat triangular muscle on the posterior proximal tibia whose fibers converge into the popliteus tendon. The popliteal vessels and tibial nerve lie behind it, and the artery normally divides at its lower border; best seen on axial and sagittal images below the plateau.
variants_pitfalls: Strain (about 1% of knee MRIs, rarely isolated): feathery edema in the belly should prompt a search for PCL, posterolateral corner, meniscal and bone injury.
Recess fluid along the tendon is sharply marginated and tubular; a strain gives ill-defined intramuscular edema or hematoma.
After a complete tendon tear the retracted belly can look like a mass; follow the tendon up before calling a soft-tissue lesion.

Aberrant anterior tibial artery (about 2–3%): a high division with the artery running in front of popliteus on the tibial cortex, best seen on axial images at the PCL attachment. Report it before osteotomy, PCL or posterolateral reconstruction, root repair or arthroplasty.
